title: fix: keep temporary filename overrides inside their directory
body:
Related: #154370

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes temporary paths escaping their chosen directory when a plugin supplies a UUID override containing path separators. Downloaded artifact names also avoid reserved Windows device basenames.

## User Impact

The temp-path SDK rejects unsafe UUID overrides. Relative `tmpDir` spelling, trimmed or blank UUIDs, compound extensions, original download metadata, and owned cleanup behavior are preserved. For example, a registry artifact named `NUL.tgz` is staged locally as `NUL_.tgz` while its original metadata stays intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the released fs-safe 0.18.0 filename helpers as the shared owner, removing 17 production lines. OpenClaw retains its existing temp-root selection and private workspace lifecycle.

The original four-file naming patch is byte-for-byte unchanged. The current signed integration head is `de3802e7a5e967794cfeb357cd6903a7c6c39741`, merging main `473d38b61bf36dac27f6977434bb060eb3d7356b`.

## Evidence

- Fresh proof on that exact head: **57/57 cases passed**, with no unhandled errors, across the SDK (15), ClawHub (30), and iMessage (12) suites. One-worker wall time was **76.293 seconds**, including 36.108 seconds preparing workers. Vitest project durations were 2.91 seconds, 4.37 seconds, and 51.80 seconds respectively.
- Real filesystem fixtures verify safe names, file bytes, integrity, metadata preservation, and workspace cleanup. iMessage retains its cleanup and authority assertions with mocked SSH/SCP.
- The four unsafe-UUID regressions and ClawHub local-name assertion were previously shown to fail on the original code. The original SDK allowed `uuid: "../../../escaped"` to escape the requested root.
- The earlier 73-case result remains attributed to the previous integration head `50c86b96d4df8252c9eb36806eeb3d1cca9135ea`. It included separate approval-fixture suites. The prior 33 selected static checks and independent P2 review cover the unchanged authored patch; they were not rerun or relabeled as current-head proof. Final source hashes and `git diff --check` passed. Current-head hosted gates remain required.

The fresh run used macOS, Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.4.0, and fs-safe/native 0.18.0 after a frozen install of the merged lockfile. Main also updated Anthropic SDK to 0.125.0, Clack core/prompts to 1.5.1/1.8.1, file-type to 22.1.0, zod to 4.6.5, and aimock to 1.42.0. These are inherited main changes; the authored naming patch is unchanged.

The integration includes the landed [session-fixture drainage and maintenance-completion repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/48883d72753bfe7f90ce6871b2cc8b41b9c789da), [archive cancellation and requester-fixture isolation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155153), and [Survivor fixture repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6ee9578ab7bfd16f219e7fd7a3b1b34292552c36). Each has separate owner proof. The historical CI cascade of 128 failed cases and 52 unhandled errors remains only partially explained; the fresh naming proof does not attribute that entire cascade to one repair.

Local proof does not claim live Windows execution, a live SSH transfer, or any operator Gateway/state mutation.
